A_general.open_code_note: The public repository is an explicitly outdated local stdio server using API v3 keys. Ahrefs says local setup is no longer supported; this code is not the hosted OAuth-protected endpoint analyzed here.
other_official_servers: The discontinued local stdio package @ahrefs/mcp is a separate server variant; it uses an API key and is explicitly unsupported for new local setups.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP fee is stated; access requires a paid Lite-or-higher subscription. MCP calls consume shared monthly API units; the help article states a minimum of 50 units per call. The endpoint documentation says new OAuth-created MCP keys default to a 200,000-unit monthly key limit, adjustable by workspace admins.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The pricing page lists Lite at $129/month, Standard at $249/month, Advanced at $449/month, and Enterprise at $1,499/month with annual commitment; listed prices and included limits may vary by billing terms.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The MCP itself has no additional fee per the help article. API units are shared across MCP, Ahrefs Connect, and direct API v3 usage. The help article lists 200,000 units/month and 100 max rows/request for Lite; 800,000 and 250 for Standard; 2,000,000 and 500 for Advanced; Enterprise is custom with unlimited rows. The introduction says enterprise customers may purchase additional units.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Lite plan or higher; plan row limits and monthly API-unit limits apply. OAuth consent is required for account connection. Enterprise customers may also connect using API keys. Workspace admins can change or remove the default OAuth-created key limit.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Ahrefs controls plan access and per-plan limits; workspace admins control the per-key monthly limit; the account holder authorizes the AI client.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The hosted endpoint exposes tool groups. Official docs say all tools are advertised if the `tools` URL parameter is omitted; comma-separated group names can select groups, and `essentials` is a standalone selection. Documentation and rendering helpers are always included. The docs do not publish individual tool names or schemas. Catalogues list 135 and 140 tools, while the Claude connector directory lists 61.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unknown for the hosted endpoint. The catalogue lists data retrieval and UI-rendering tools but does not establish the hosted result/error wire format.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: The endpoint's supplied OAuth metadata advertises scope `apiv3-mcp`. The authorization-server metadata lists authorization code and implicit grants, authorization endpoint https://app.ahrefs.com/web/oauth/authorize, token endpoint https://ahrefs.com/oauth/token, registration endpoint https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/register, and PKCE method S256. The endpoint POST returned HTTP 400 `Blank input data`; the separate endpoint-existence test reported HTTP 401. Metadata does not provide token lifetime, revocation behavior, or token authentication methods. Docs describe an authorization consent screen and an account API key tagged with `MCP` scope.

The hosted endpoint accepts a `tools` query parameter to select available tool groups. If omitted, all groups are advertised. `essentials` must be used alone; unknown groups are rejected. Helpers for documentation and rendering remain included regardless of selected groups.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The reviewed hosted docs describe data reports, management, and public endpoint groups; no tool annotations or individual official tool list are published. Catalogue-listed tools are predominantly data reads and UI rendering. 2. No server-enforced confirmation flow or MCP Elicitation documented; OAuth consent is documented for account authorization. 3. Supplied OAuth scope is `apiv3-mcp`; docs say the account connection creates a dedicated API key tagged `MCP` scope. The endpoint docs set a default 200,000-unit/month key limit adjustable by workspace admins. Inherited product role, allowlists, redirect approval, token lifetime, and revocation details: Unknown. 4. Docs document group filters through `?tools=...`; all groups are advertised by default, `essentials` is standalone, unknown groups are rejected. Read-only mode, sandbox/production selection, and regional endpoints: Unknown. 5. No MCP-specific field masking, PII exclusion, or data boundary behavior found. 6. Plan row limits and monthly units apply; help page states minimum 50 units per call. Unit limits are shared with Ahrefs Connect and direct API. No hosted result truncation behavior found. 7. Hosted argument validation/correction behavior: Unknown; unknown tool groups are rejected. 8. Hosted MCP logging/audit/telemetry behavior: Unknown. Account usage can be viewed in settings. 9. No vendor feedback/rating tools identified among the catalogue names/descriptions. No hosted upsell-result behavior or agent marketing instructions found. 10. No server-delivered skills or behavioral instructions found. Documentation gives client setup instructions and tool grouping guidance. 11. Memory/state effects: Unknown. 12. One hosted endpoint with selectable tool groups; no evidence of nested server or proxy architecture. 13. No raw arbitrary API request, SQL, script, or execute tool identified in the catalogue tool list.

D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: One hosted endpoint with optional tool-group selection is documented; this does not establish a multi-server or nested architecture.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: Official hosted documentation exists at https://docs.ahrefs.com/en/mcp/docs/tool-categories and documents 17 selectable groups plus always-included documentation/rendering helpers, but it publishes no individual tool names or stated total. actions.json contains the 135 named tools listed by Composio's Ahrefs MCP catalogue. Names are labelled third-party because the official docs do not name them individually. The Claude connector directory lists 61 tools and exposes a partial name list; Agent Discoverability lists 140; these catalogue totals differ. No MCP schemas were published in the inspected official or catalogue text, so parameters are marked NOT PUBLISHED.

E_aggregated.token_method: The only public code is a separate, outdated local server; hosted tool definitions and initialize instructions were not available verbatim.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The full Ahrefs software includes additional features beyond the documented MCP tool groups, such as site auditing, content tooling, social media management, and other products. The hosted docs do not provide an exhaustive human-versus-MCP operation matrix, so specific unavailable operations are NOT FOUND. The public REST API reference documents additional API endpoints but its parameters were not treated as MCP tool parameters.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The docs instruct clients to choose `tools` groups and warn that unsupported group names are rejected. They do not state that the server enforces recommendations to the AI beyond connection/configuration validation. The external endpoint is described as unsupported for use through custom scripts, bridges, or standalone HTTP/JSON-RPC clients.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The help article says: "Your data is only shared with the AI client you have specifically configured on your local machine." This is a vendor statement, not a described server-side data-protection mechanism. The general privacy policy and terms were reviewed; no MCP-specific retention, training, or masking statement was located.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The introduction describes the hosted server as allowing AI agents to securely access Ahrefs API data. It documents OAuth authorization and dedicated MCP-tagged API keys, plus usage tracking and configurable per-key unit limits.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth metadata substantiates protected-resource authorization and the docs describe consent and key limits. The per-key limit is configurable by workspace admins. No inspected source describes technical enforcement of the help article's data-sharing promise, data masking, retention, or AI-training policy specifically for MCP.

contradictions: Tool counts differ across catalogues: Composio lists 135, Agent Discoverability lists 140, and Claude's connector directory states 61 tools. Official Ahrefs docs provide tool groups but no individual names or total, so these totals cannot be reconciled against an official manifest.

The supplied OAuth metadata advertises scope `apiv3-mcp`, while Ahrefs docs describe API keys tagged with `MCP` scope. The supplied authorization-server metadata also advertises the implicit grant alongside authorization code and S256 PKCE.

The endpoint POST response in the supplied metadata was HTTP 400 `Blank input data`, whereas the separate connection test reported HTTP 401. These are distinct probes and neither supplied an MCP tool manifest.
observations_for_research: Ahrefs documents a URL query parameter that controls groups of advertised tools, with all groups on by default and an `essentials` preset.
Tool-group selection is a client-facing exposure control; the docs state that documentation and rendering helpers remain available regardless of selection.
The endpoint is metered through shared API units and has plan-dependent result-row caps; OAuth-created MCP keys have an adjustable monthly unit limit.
notes: Reviewed the supplied links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ bundle, OAuth metadata, and local public repository. The repo is an archived/outdated local stdio implementation, not the deployed hosted server; no hosted implementation code was found. The NPM page returned HTTP 403 in the evidence bundle. Official hosted pages publish tool groups but no complete individual list or schemas; actions.json therefore uses catalogue names/descriptions and marks parameters NOT PUBLISHED. Catalogue disagreement is recorded above. The official docs-search pages concern documentation, not the product endpoint.
